entities.name: object imported from a module of another language

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module IS the top-level unit of TTCN-3.
requirements.original: The top-level unit of TTCN-3 is a module.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module CANNOT be structured into sub-modules.
requirements.original: A module cannot be structured into sub-modules.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module MAY import definitions from other modules.
requirements.original: A module can import definitions from other modules.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module MAY have module parameters to allow test suite parameterization.
requirements.original: Modules can have module parameters to allow test suite parameterization.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module IS a set of definitions of test components, communication ports, other kinds of types, constants, templates, functions including the module control function, signatures for procedure calls at ports and test cases.
requirements.original: A module consists of a set of definitions that define test components, communication ports, other kinds of types (see clause 6), constants, test data templates, functions including the module control function, signatures for procedure calls at ports, test cases, etc.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control function calls the test cases and controls their execution.
requirements.original: The module control function calls the test cases and controls their execution.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control function MAY declare local variables.
requirements.original: The control function may also declare (local) variables, etc.

requirements.subject: ent:program-statement
requirements.canonical: Program statements (such as if-else and do-while) CAN be used in the module control function to specify the selection and execution order of individual test cases.
requirements.original: Program statements (such as if-else and do-while) can be used to specify the selection and execution order of individual test cases.

requirements.subject: ent:global-variable
requirements.canonical: Global variables ARE NOT supported in TTCN-3; a variable SHALL NOT be declared directly in the module definitions part.
requirements.original: The concept of global variables is not supported in TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:basic-type
requirements.canonical: TTCN-3 predefined basic types include integer, float, boolean, verdicttype and the string types.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 has a number of predefined data types that include basic types (such as integer, float, boolean, verdicttype and string types) as well as structured types (such as records, sets, unions, enumerated and map types and arrays).

requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: TTCN-3 structured types include record, set, union, enumerated and map types and arrays.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 has a number of predefined data types that include basic types (such as integer, float, boolean, verdicttype and string types) as well as structured types (such as records, sets, unions, enumerated and map types and arrays).

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template IS a special kind of data structure that provides parameterization and matching mechanisms for specifying test data to be sent or received over ports.
requirements.original: A special kind of data structure called a template provides parameterization and matching mechanisms for specifying test data to be sent or received over the test ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: The operations on ports provide message-based and procedure-based communication capabilities.
requirements.original: The operations on these ports provide both message-based and procedure-based communication capabilities.

requirements.subject: ent:signature
requirements.canonical: Procedure calls MAY be used for testing implementations which are not message based.
requirements.original: Procedure calls may be used for testing implementations which are not message based.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: Dynamic test behaviour IS expressed as test cases.
requirements.original: Dynamic test behaviour is expressed as test cases.

requirements.subject: ent:program-statement
requirements.canonical: TTCN-3 program statements include behaviour description mechanisms for alternative reception of communication and timer events, interleaving and default behaviour.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 program statements include powerful behaviour description mechanisms such as alternative reception of communication and timer events, interleaving and default behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: TTCN-3 supports test verdict assignment and logging mechanisms.
requirements.original: Test verdict assignment and logging mechanisms are also supported.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 language element MAY be assigned attributes such as encoding information and display attributes.
requirements.original: Finally, TTCN-3 language elements may be assigned attributes such as encoding information and display attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: A user MAY specify non-standardized user-defined attributes.
requirements.original: It is also possible to specify (non-standardized) user-defined attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: The notions "definition" and "declaration" of variables, constants, types and other language elements ARE used interchangeably and have equal meaning on the level of TTCN-3.
requirements.original: NOTE: The notions "definition" and "declaration" of variables, constants, types and other language elements are used interchangeably throughout the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 identifier IS case sensitive.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 identifiers are case sensitive.

requirements.subject: ent:keyword
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 keyword SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 keywords shall be written in all lowercase letters (see annex A).

requirements.subject: ent:keyword
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 keyword SHALL NOT be used as identifier of a TTCN-3 object.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 keywords shall neither be used as identifiers of TTCN-3 objects nor as identifiers of objects imported from modules of other languages.

requirements.subject: ent:keyword
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 keyword SHALL NOT be used as identifier of an object imported from a module of another language.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 keywords shall neither be used as identifiers of TTCN-3 objects nor as identifiers of objects imported from modules of other languages.

requirements.subject: ent:predefined-function
requirements.canonical: The name of a predefined TTCN-3 function SHALL NOT be used as identifier of a TTCN-3 object.
requirements.original: The same rules apply to names of predefined TTCN-3 functions (see annex C).

ambiguity.issue: "The same rules" may refer only to the preceding sentence (prohibition of use as identifiers) or also to the lowercase rule of 5.1-s002; the identifier prohibition was chosen as it is the immediately preceding rule.
readings: The name of a predefined TTCN-3 function SHALL NOT be used as identifier of a TTCN-3 object or of an imported object.
The name of a predefined TTCN-3 function SHALL be written in lowercase letters and SHALL NOT be used as identifier of a TTCN-3 object or of an imported object.

requirements.subject: ent:predefined-function
requirements.canonical: The name of a predefined TTCN-3 function SHALL NOT be used as identifier of an object imported from a module of another language.
requirements.original: The same rules apply to names of predefined TTCN-3 functions (see annex C).

requirements.subject: ent:modifier
requirements.canonical: A special TTCN-3 modifier IS an identifier prefixed with the @-symbol.
requirements.original: Special TTCN-3 modifiers are identifiers prefixed with the @-symbol (see annex A).

requirements.subject: ent:modifier
requirements.canonical: A modifier modifies the default semantics of the language element it is applied to in the specified way.
requirements.original: They modify the default semantics of the language element they are applied to in the specified way.

requirements.subject: ent:modifier
requirements.condition: more than one modifier is applied to a language element
requirements.canonical: If more than one modifier is applied to a language element, the modifiers MAY be applied in any order.
requirements.original: If more than one modifier is applied to a language element, they may be applied in any order.

requirements.subject: ent:modifier
requirements.canonical: A modifier CANNOT lead to backward incompatibilities with existing reserved keywords or identifiers.
requirements.original: NOTE: These modifiers are useful for refining or modifying existing language features, for example in the context of the optional extension packages of TTCN-3 since they cannot lead to backward incompatibilities with existing reserved keywords or identifiers.
